newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares end higher, weaker PT cuts gains.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares end higher, weaker PT cuts gains.

text.p: 1640 GMT - Portuguese shares ended higher, but the weaker close of Portugal Telecom on Lisbon bourse as it adjusted to the New York stock price limited overall gains. Futures on PT also fell.
* The rise of New York and European markets helped the Lisbon bourse to recover previous losses, dealers said.

* The Lisbon bourse was expected to react tomorrow, with other European bourses, to remarks by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan at 1800 GMT on the U.S. economy. "The trend in the local market tomorrow is very dependent on today's speech by Greenspan and the effect it will have an the U.S. market," a dealer said.

* Shares in Portuguese bank Banco Espirito Santo (BES) reacted positively to a 43 percent increase in consolidated net profit in the first half of 1997, but the shares did not surpass the 4,500 escudo level reached early in the session before the release of the result. BES closed at 4,498 escudos, up 83, in turnover of 675,817 shares.

* Portugal's largest private bank, Banco Comercial Portugues, presents its six-month results at 1700 GMT. The reaction of the local market will be felt tomorrow. Analysts expect BCP to post a profit of between 13 and 13.5 billion escudos.
